summary: Neil (Couch Investor) joins a Motley Fool host to cover three stocks that have run up hard but still have durable growth stories. The host pitches TransDigm (TDG): a $61B aerospace sole-source parts compounder (~90% of portfolio FAA-certified sole-source, 60% gross / 46% operating margins) down 17.6% YTD on regulatory scrutiny, calling it 'an interesting time to buy on the dip' while flagging its deliberate ~$34B debt load (5.8x net debt/EBITDA). Neil discusses Micron at length: HBM sold out for 2026, 80%+ gross margins, single-digit forward P/E, with the AI memory super-cycle structurally changing the industry's boom-bust profile — positive but no new explicit call beyond his standing BUY. The host pitches Marvell (MRVL) as a buy-and-hold: custom AI silicon for AWS/Microsoft/Google (Google warrant for up to 7%), record $2.8B quarterly revenue (+40%), data center 80% of mix; Neil agrees it's a 'pure growth story' with 40%+ revenue growth guided but makes no explicit call himself. No stance flips for Couch Investor.
